core_obligations: Forward direction: for an H-torsor F, form the free abelian sheaf Z[F], note that the augmentation sigma : Z[F] -> Z has kernel generated by sections [s] - [s'], use the canonical map a : Ker(sigma) -> H sending [s] - [s'] to the element h with h s' = s, and take the pushout of 0 -> Ker(sigma) -> Z[F] -> Z -> 0 along a; the resulting short exact sequence gives a class xi_F in H^1(X, H) as the boundary of 1 in H^0(X, Z) (proof lines 276-309).

Converse direction: given xi in H^1(X, H), choose an embedding H contained in I into an injective abelian sheaf, set Q = I/H, and use H^1(X, I) = 0 to write xi as the image of a global section q of Q; then the subsheaf F contained in I of sections mapping to q is a torsor (proof lines 312-331).

Establish the bijection: the two constructions displayed as pushout and pullback of a short exact sequence are mutually inverse, which the author states and leaves to the reader, completing the claimed canonical bijection (proof lines 333-335).
proof_roadmap: Send a torsor to a class by pushing the extension 0 -> Ker(sigma) -> Z[F] -> Z -> 0 out along Ker(sigma) -> H and applying the boundary map to 1 (proof lines 276-309).
Recover a torsor from a class by embedding H in an injective I, using H^1(X, I) = 0 to lift the class to a global section q of I/H, and taking the subsheaf of I mapping to q (proof lines 312-331).
Note that the two constructions are mutually inverse, a verification the author omits and which is reproduced as written (proof lines 333-335).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states a canonical bijection between isomorphism classes of H-torsors and H^1(X, H) for an abelian sheaf H on a topological space (statement lines 269-272). Both directions are genuine constructions: a torsor is sent to a class through the free abelian sheaf it generates, the augmentation to Z, the map [s] - [s'] -> h with h s' = s on the kernel and the resulting pushout, whose boundary on 1 in H^0(X, Z) gives the class (proof lines 276-309); conversely a class is recovered as a torsor by embedding H in an injective sheaf I, using the vanishing of H^1(X, I) to lift the class to a global section q of I/H, and taking the subsheaf of I mapping to q (proof lines 312-331). The author leaves the double-composition check to the reader and that sentence is reproduced as written. The claim is H2: two explicit constructions over one small exact sequence.
